dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #Everything in the forest will never be forgotten. Nara {NICKNAME}, your story will pass on and on among Aranara, Araja knows that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Marana...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: It's a story from very long ago...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: A long time ago, Aranara walked the earth and made friends with Nara and all living creatures. There was no Marana then. Until a disaster that occurred many, many moons ago...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata returned to Sarva, and the Marana's rampage through the earth began. Once the forest recovered its vitality, the Aranara hid the real Vanarana in a dream to protect themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: The forest didn't know death, until a day came when the trees realized that withered flowers and dead animals covered the earth.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: On the same day, the earth remembered the dark, poisonous blood it had once devoured, or was about to devour. The rivers thought of the descent of the sun, evaporating all water and leaving a red world behind.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: They realized that all things would meet their end, and so, Marana was born. It is the name of death, and those who know it shall die.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Marana urges everything towards death. As for the tall, dark, and warped beings, they are the avatars chosen by Marana, the heralds of death.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: ...Now that you defeated Marana's Avatar with Arama, and the forest sees another Ashvattha, everything should take a turn for the better.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Aranyaka...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Nara Varuna left this, and Arama is giving it to you. Arama thinks he did the right thing.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: It's filled with stories between you and Aranara, right? Araja knows that Nara will forget about how to dream, and forget about us.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: However, as long as the Aranyaka keeps the records of our stories and names, you can always read it without the memories about Aranara.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: When that day comes, Araja hopes you will find these stories interesting and touching.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Arama...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Araja misses him very much. With Arama turning into the new Ashvattha, Araja's dreams have become quieter.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: The time when Nara and Aranara spend time together, and walk the shades together. Araja can't recall anything like that, but stories remain.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Araja was hoping, Arama could see a similar world as a seed. But everything ends up in Sarva, where Nara and Aranara will be joined.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #Also, Araja is delighted, for the friendship between Arama and Nara {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Arana...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Arana is also an ancient Aranara, with so many blooms and rainfall captured in memories.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Because of the overflowing love for Nara and the forest, Arana refuses to be Vasara Tree. Vasara Tree, can't play with Nara.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Araja heard that, Arana and Narana went traveling together. All the stories and beautiful things on the trip, hopefully, will make up for Arana's loss.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Goodbye. If anything ever tires you, come for a rest.
